No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

A plan, an elevation and a small set of terms are enough to begin reading a temple. The lecture compares the northern, southern and Deccan traditions through photographs and drawings. For a fuller treatment, see the four-session course on Indian temple architecture.

Length, level and language are agreed with you. The lecture can be given online or at your venue, for a single class, a department or a whole organisation.

What it covers

  • The parts of a temple, from gateway to sanctum
  • Nāgara, Drāviḍa and Vesara: how to tell them apart
  • Reading a plan and an elevation
  • Examples from north India, the south and the Deccan

How the time is spent

  1. Reading plan 30 min

    Locate axis, entrance, hall and sanctum.

    You: label plan

  2. Reading elevation 20 min

    Identify shikhara or vimana forms.

    You: annotate elevation

  3. Reading images 20 min

    Connect iconography and architectural setting.

    You: observation table

  4. Mini case discussion 20 min

    Explain uncertainties and conservation context.

    You: three-minute reading

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Identify the parts of a temple, from gateway to sanctum, on a plan.
  • Distinguish the Nāgara, Drāviḍa and Vesara traditions using photographs and drawings.
  • Read a temple elevation and identify its shikhara or vimana form.
